response: The treatment of amblyopia does not significantly change or normalize subfoveal choroidal thickness in amblyopic children. Although a six-month treatment of amblyopia can increase the visual acuity of the anisometropic hyperopic amblyopic eyes, it does not have a significant impact on choroidal thickness. This suggests that the pathophysiology of amblyopia is more closely related to abnormalities in the visual cortex and lateral geniculate nucleus, rather than changes in choroidal thickness.
